name: Anonymized creative-work payment review for DPRK IT-worker risk

attribution.legal_posture: Anonymized risk-review examples cover candidate-risk patterns; DPRK attribution, blocked-payment findings, criminal cases, sanctions designations, labor determinations and immigration actions fall outside the examples.

caveats: Anime or creative-work contractors from Yanji or Dandong require separate evidence before any DPRK-linked status is recorded.
Publish only the control lesson: verify contractual identity, work provenance, counterparty purpose and payment continuity using lawful internal data.
Review was prompted by concern; payee DPRK-worker status remains unconfirmed.

The anonymized Yanji individual and Dandong company have source-level context only; geography and work type are contextual, and DPRK-worker or front-company classification, identification, and profiling require source-specific evidence.

infrastructure.statement: Japan's 2025 proliferation-financing risk assessment publishes two anonymized examples supplied through domestic financial institutions. One concerned a yen remittance to an individual in Yanji for an anime-drawing request; the other concerned a yen remittance to a company in Dandong for an anime drawing. In both examples, geographic context and the stated digital-service purpose prompted additional customer, counterparty or compliance review because of concern about DPRK IT workers.

sources.support: The underlying assessment was published on December 22, 2025; this URL is the English translation file published/file-dated April 30, 2026. The underlying Japanese assessment was published on December 22, 2025; this URL is the official provisional English translation dated April 30, 2026. Japan assesses that DPRK IT workers have impersonated Japanese citizens to earn income through online work-order platforms. Two anonymized financial-institution examples describe enhanced review of yen payments labeled for anime-drawing work to an individual in Yanji and a company in Dandong because of DPRK IT-worker risk
sources.locator: Report pp. 43-44 and Table 3, examples 2-3, report p. 81
